gaps.sentence: Many people fell asleep ___ the lecture.
gaps.hint: within the period of an event
gaps.explanation: 'During' is followed by a noun (the lecture) and means within that time; 'while' needs a clause with a verb.
'Valuable' means worth a lot of money; 'valued' means appreciated; 'invaluable' already means priceless, so it is not graded.

gaps.sentence: Teenagers ___ hours every day on social media.
gaps.hint: to use time or money on something (neutral)
gaps.explanation: 'Spend time/money on something' is the neutral verb for using time or money; 'waste' implies useless use.

gaps.sentence: She has had a brilliant ___ in politics.
gaps.hint: the whole course of a person's professional life
gaps.explanation: 'Career' is the progress through a working life, especially in one profession; 'job' is one position.

gaps.sentence: One of the bolts had worked ___ in the vibration.
gaps.explanation: 'Work loose' = become untightened; 'lose' is the verb for misplacing.

gaps.sentence: He ___ on the sofa all afternoon yesterday.
gaps.explanation: 'Lay' is the past of 'lie' (recline): he lay on the sofa. 'Laid' would need an object.

gaps.sentence: I was so ___ when I forgot her name in front of everyone.
gaps.hint: how you feel in an awkward social situation
gaps.explanation: 'Embarrassed' describes short-term discomfort in a social situation; 'ashamed' implies guilt about wrongdoing.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
